summary: Your Instagram Reels are doing far better than YouTube Shorts: most Reels get 1,000+ views, while most Shorts get under 100. The best videos are short, surprising claims about a sensor or robot (like 'Clap Switch only listens to noise' or 'Robot falls without a gyro'), which get views, likes, saves and shares. Generic 'How does X work?' questions on everyday devices (smoke alarm, tap, lift, mall door) get few views and little engagement.
winningPattern: Hindi Reels on Instagram about a robot or a simple Arduino-style sensor (clap switch, gyro, line follower, IR, mic, heat sensor). The title makes a surprising or 'it can't do what you think' claim, like 'X doesn't see/hear, it only does Y' or 'Without X the robot falls', with a robot or clap/sound demo and a short punchy Hindi line. Published in late October to early November, with emoji and #shorts.
doMore: Make robot and maker-module videos (gyro, line follower, IR, mic, clap switch) with a surprising claim in the title
Use the 'X doesn't do what you think, it only does Y' hook, which shows up in most top videos
Post to Instagram first and treat it as the main platform; it brings roughly 10x the views
Make follow-ups to winners, such as a clap switch part 3 or a gyro balance demo, with a new angle each time
Add a clear question or challenge near the end to push saves and shares, since shares were highest on the IR robot video
stopDoing: Generic 'X kaise kaam karta hai?' titles on everyday devices like taps, lifts, mall doors and smoke alarms
Posting several near-duplicate videos on one topic (smoke detector, IR in the dark, washroom tap) that split the audience and get low views
Posting English or Hindi videos on YouTube only, with no Instagram version, since those got almost no reach
